# Feature Specification: The external floor runs the code-review lines

## The pipelines

_(Amended 2026-10-26, #3502.)_ `fix-ci`, which also repairs a red round as `repair-build`, runs on `gemini-4-argon`: on loop-bench's medium and large tickets (HALEngine #37, #94, #95, #144) Argon left 38 of 68 repairs green and Gemini 3.1 Pro 18 of 66, all 18 on #95 and none on the other three. The definition of done stays on `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` and `tdd-round` on `claude-sonnet-4-6`, since the bench has compared models for them on the smallest ticket only; the choice is revisited when it has the rest. ([validated by runs the implementation loop on gemini-3.1-pro-preview except tdd-round on claude-sonnet-4-6 and fix-ci on gemini-4-argon, review and re-check on gemini-4-argon and the reply on clau…

- **`loop-fix-ci` moves to `gemini-4-argon`.** It is the one agent behind both repair steps, after a red round (`repair-build`) and after review (`fix-ci`). Argon's repairs took 4 minutes at the median and 22 at most, so the 45-minute limit stays. Its price is $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, with cache reads at $0.20. That launch price doubles after 2026-11-30.
- **The definition of done stays on Gemini 3.1 Pro, and `tdd-round` on Sonnet 4.6.** The bench has compared models for them on the smallest ticket only. Cheap models that look good there fall apart on larger tickets: Haiku 5.5's `tdd-round` went green in 22 of 28 runs on #93 but only 6 of 46 on #94.
- One caveat: the bench's repair is not all of production's `fix-ci`, which also answers review comments.

## What happens

Each did this on both attempts, so the loop ended on `retry_budget` in about a minute. The other seven models (gpt-5.6-*, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, Gemini 3 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon) skipped the calls and reached green.

## Why it matters in production

Pods normally have the Lore MCP, but not always reliably: the first-round `round-brief.md` never exists, and a gateway hiccup or a vendor that does not receive the MCP config (see re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem#241) leaves the tools missing. A model that follows the prompt to the letter then fails the round instead of doing the work, and a failed round twice ends the ticket.
